question: Can I use this example in the AI tool I intend to test?
help: Check the permissions and data rules that apply to your actual tool. A fictional or approved example may let you test without sharing restricted information.

source.section: Three Ways to Work with AI

routingGuidance: If permission is unclear, keep the live task untested and prepare an approved example first.

question: What happened when I actually tried this task?
help: Record a result from an attempt, with the tool or model, date and enough detail to understand what was tried. An expectation is not a test result.
routingGuidance: A missing attempt stays untested. Do not infer success from confidence or a similar task.

question: What was usable, and what had to be corrected?
help: Separate the quality of the first output from the effort needed to reach an acceptable result. Note failures as well as successes.

source.section: Three Ways to Work with AI

question: What would happen if an important part were wrong?
help: Name the consequence and how you would notice it. Higher stakes call for stronger evidence and evaluation, rather than an automatic assumption that either humans or AI are always safer.

question: What would I realistically do without AI help?
help: Compare with the help, time and expertise you can actually obtain. The relevant alternative might be an expert, doing it yourself, delay or getting no assistance.

question: How will I tell whether the result is good enough?
help: Identify a source, observable test or person with the expertise to judge the important parts. An agent’s own assurance is not that check.

source.section: When You’re the Expert and Can Judge Fast

routingGuidance: If you cannot evaluate the important parts, find appropriate help, narrow the task or remain undecided.

question: What skill or judgment do I want to keep developing here?
help: Completion and learning can require different ways of using AI. Name any part you want to attempt, explain or practice yourself.

question: Does my own thinking, voice or involvement carry part of the value?
help: Consider the purpose and the relationship. A boundary can cover one part of a task and can change later; it is not a claim of permanent human superiority.

question: Where do I need to stay involved while the work happens?
help: Separate a clear division of labor from close collaboration and agent execution. One task can use different modes for different parts.

source.section: Three Ways to Work with AI

question: What result and constraints would I give an agent?
help: Write the goal, necessary context, allowed changes, required outputs and evidence of completion. Keep requirements concrete enough to evaluate.

source.section: Three Ways to Work with AI

question: Which actions need my review, and what must the agent leave to me?
help: Set boundaries and any necessary checkpoints around consequences you cannot cheaply undo. Continuous supervision is not required for every delegated task.

source.section: Three Ways to Work with AI

routingGuidance: These fields operationalize the brief’s oversight requirement; they are not a fourth working mode attributed to the book.

question: Does delegation still help after instructions, review and rework?
help: Use what you observed rather than counting generation speed alone. Include failed attempts and whether you would prefer to do the task yourself.

source.section: Three Ways to Work with AI

question: Who or what depends on this output next?
help: Check whether faster or more numerous outputs will improve the final outcome or create another queue. You may need to coordinate beyond your own task.

source.section: O-Rings, Garbage Cans, and Dissolving Walls

question: Will this arrangement leave me able to choose priorities and stop?
help: Consider the review workload, the pace of work and who benefits. A technically effective arrangement can still need a different boundary.

source.section: Three Ways to Work with AI

question: What new evidence would make me revisit this choice?
help: A changed model, different stakes, new learning goals or a failure can matter before a scheduled reminder. Treat a decision as revisable.
